name: advance_lighting_phase_and_intensity
description: Advances the phase bytes of several light structures, wrapping them at fixed limits, and steps a 16-bit intensity value down by a fixed amount or up toward a maximum depending on a flag. It then clamps the intensity into a third structure's state and copies a table value into a fourth when the intensity is at or above a threshold.

name: init_timer_flags_and_state
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global block pointer, then zeroes several flags and loads a timing counter with a fixed starting value. It sets one state byte to 4, or to 4 or 0 depending on a bit test of a value returned by another routine.

name: advance_light_sequence_spawn_entity
description: Counts down a light timer and steps the state bytes of up to three structures, toggling a parity bit when the timer expires. When the sequence is enabled it allocates a free entry from a table of 40 slots, fills its fields from global values and a lookup table, and points its callback at the handler routine.

name: reset_timer_and_entity_flags
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global block pointer, then sets an active flag, loads a countdown of 1250, sets two further flags to their starting values, and zeroes the state byte of each of two structures.

name: update_light_timers_and_cycles
description: Counts down a light timer and, when a reload counter expires, toggles a light's state bit and recalculates the reload from the remaining time. When the gate flag is clear it resets the light states to their idle values and clears the sequence; it then advances two cyclic counters that wrap at fixed limits.

name: copy_byte_flag_if_changed
description: Copies a global byte into a byte field of a structure referenced by a global pointer, and sets the structure's flag byte to one, only when the two values differ.

name: clear_light_state_variables
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global block pointer, then zeroes three global variables and the state byte of each of two structures referenced by global pointers.

name: clamp_states_and_decay_counters
description: Clamps two global values to a maximum of four and writes them into the state bytes of two structures when they differ. It also decreases two global counters by two, stopping each at zero.

name: reset_tracking_counters_and_flags
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global block pointer, then zeroes three counters, sets two flags to one, and writes the values zero, zero, three and zero into the state bytes of four structures.

name: advance_two_bit_cycle
description: When both a flag and a counter are nonzero, advances a two-bit cycle byte in one structure, wrapping at four, and marks that structure as changed. The counter is cleared when the cycle wraps back to zero.

name: advance_cycle_and_step_handler
description: Advances a two-bit cycle byte when a flag and a counter are both nonzero, marking the structure as changed. It also counts down a global index and, while it is nonzero, stores a handler routine address from a lookup table into a structure and a matching byte from a second table into another.

name: decrement_index_store_handler
description: Decrements an index passed in a register and stores it in a global. It then writes a handler routine address and a table byte into two structures referenced by an address register, marking the first as changed, and returns the register value with its low two bits set.

name: reset_flags_set_states
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global block pointer, then clears six global flags. If a counter is below ten it zeroes two state bytes; otherwise it sets one state byte to 4 or 0 from a bit test of a called routine's result and sets the other to 4 when the first is 4.

name: step_state_toward_target
description: Either decrements a pending delay counter or, once it reaches zero, steps one state byte up or down within the range zero to four according to a second state byte. It then copies both state bytes into two global variables.

name: clear_counters_and_state_bytes
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global block pointer, then zeroes two global counters and the state byte of each of two structures referenced by global pointers.

name: advance_triple_cycle_counters
description: Advances the state bytes of two structures whose enable flags are set, wrapping each back to zero at three and clearing its enable flag on wrap. Both structures are marked as changed on every update.

name: initialize_pointers_and_clear_flags
description: Stores four values returned by a called routine into global pointers when a flag is zero, then calls the shared setup routine. It runs a six-step sequence of routine calls when a count exceeds one, and finally clears several globals and the state byte of every structure in a sentinel-terminated pointer table; its referenced strings name the back, drop, plane and shower graphics files.

name: advance_door_animation_sequence
description: Advances a six-step cycle byte for a door and copies it into two linked structures, then counts down a frame timer. When an animation sequence completes it writes twelve table entries into sprite fields and allocates a new entity from a table of 40 slots, with parameters taken from the cycle byte.

name: start_sequence_from_parameter
description: When a global sequence flag is clear, stores the low word of the argument as the current sequence index and computes a paired value from a byte table indexed by a counter and that index. It does nothing while the flag is set.

name: load_sequence_index_from_entry
description: Reads the sequence index from a field of the structure at the current address register, stores it in the sequence index global, and computes the paired table value as the sibling start routine does, without checking any flag.

name: setup_blitter_copy_from_table
description: Waits for the blitter to become idle, then computes a destination address from a table entry and programs the blitter's source and destination pointers, control registers, full-width masks and zero modulos. It then starts a fixed-size blit and is called from two other routines.

name: configure_handler_slots
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global block pointer, then sets several counters to starting values, with a global threshold of 18 choosing between minus one and zero. It clears the state bytes of every structure in a sentinel-terminated pointer table, configures six handler slots with routine addresses, sizes and positions, and its referenced text is the string NuSh.

name: advance_animation_phase_counters
description: Advances a 12-step cycle byte in one structure in one of two modes depending on a global threshold, shifting two position values and rotating a table index while a counter runs. It also steps a sequence of phases that copies bytes from a source pointer into a structure, and counts down a timer byte that clears a flag when it reaches zero.

name: advance_secondary_animation_counters
description: Applies the same phase logic to a second animation: a 12-step cycle byte in one structure, two position values that step by minus two, and a rotated table index while its counter runs. It copies source bytes into a structure through a sequence phase and counts down a timer byte that clears a flag at zero.

name: reset_flag_set_bit_state
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global block pointer, then clears a flag and the state bytes of two structures. It sets a third structure's byte to one when a global value is below four, or to a bit test of a called routine's result otherwise.

name: advance_indexed_state_table_entry
description: When an enable flag is set and a state byte is nonzero, advances a five-step cycle byte in one structure and writes successive values from a table into another, adjusting a value of seven by a modifier. The index wraps at 32, and when it reaches 18 it selects a limit of 13 or 6 depending on the modifier.

name: set_input_flags_from_thresholds
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global block pointer, then sets two flags to one below a global threshold of six, or from bit tests of called routine results at or above that threshold. It clears six state bytes and then sets or derives two more state bytes using the same global threshold of six.

name: advance_paired_cycle_counters
description: Advances a cycle byte that wraps at eight and toggles a global flag each time it returns to zero, then sets a three-step byte in another structure whose second value depends on that flag. When an active flag and an enable byte are both set, it sets a flag and advances a four-step byte and an eight-step byte in two further structures.

name: advance_secondary_entity_cycles
description: Performs the same paired cycle advance as its sibling routine on a second set of structures, toggling its own global flag at each wrap of the eight-step byte. The active branch sets a flag and advances a four-step byte and an eight-step byte in two other structures.

name: blit_sprite_rows_from_table
description: Once the global counter exceeds five, sets the blitter's destination pointer from a structure offset and waits for the blitter to be idle. It then copies three rows of four words from a global data table to the blitter, advancing the source per row, and clears two flags when the sequence index reaches six.

name: derive_states_and_store_increments
description: Below a global threshold of eight it sets two state bytes to fixed values, otherwise it sets them from bit tests of two called routine results. It then stores each state byte plus one into two global variables.

name: write_table_entries_and_counters
description: Writes successive bytes from two global tables into two structures, wrapping each index at eight. Each time an index wraps to zero a 1-to-5 counter advances, and the counter minus one is written to each structure only when it differs from the stored byte.

name: clear_counters_and_three_states
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global pointer table, then zeroes two global variables and the state byte of each of three structures.

name: load_table_values_by_index
description: Copies table bytes selected by a global index into the state bytes of two structures and advances that index modulo sixteen, setting a counter to five when the index is one. A second index copies one table byte into a third structure and advances modulo eight.

name: reset_state_bytes_and_flags
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global pointer table, then zeroes two global variables and sets five structure state bytes, the first to five and the rest to zero.

name: shift_counts_between_two_entries
description: When the current index differs from a target index, decrements a counter in the current entry if it is nonzero and increments a counter in the target entry up to five. When the target reaches five and the current entry reaches zero, the current index is moved to the target.

name: clear_entries_and_set_offsets
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global pointer table, then zeroes a flag and the state bytes of ten structures from a pointer table. It sets two global values to nine below a global threshold of twenty and to zero otherwise, and writes three times the remainder of nine minus each value, plus two, into two structure state bytes.

name: advance_frames_and_position_counters
description: Writes a cycling frame value from zero to two into eight structures listed in a pointer table and decrements one further wrapped state byte. While its countdown is active it advances two position counters that wrap at 29, dividing the countdown into rows of three by division and remainder.

name: clear_pointer_table_and_flags
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global pointer table, then zeroes four global variables, the state byte of the first four entries in a pointer table, and two more global variables.

name: clamp_states_write_table_values
description: Clamps two global values to a maximum of four and writes them into two structure state bytes when they differ. It decreases two counters by two with a floor of zero, and writes table values into two more structure bytes while their indices are nonzero, decrementing each index.

name: set_state_bytes_to_three
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global pointer table, then writes the value three into the state byte of each of two structures referenced by global pointers.

name: update_entity_flag_bits
description: Reads a flag byte from each of two structures, sets or clears bits in each according to several global flags and states, and writes both bytes back. Each byte's update combines an exclusive-or toggle with conditional bit sets.

name: configure_bounds_for_threshold
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global pointer table. Below a global threshold of 26 it sets two bounds to a fixed value, sets two state bytes to fixed values and marks a flag; otherwise it derives both bounds from called routine results masked to three bits and multiplied by 204, then clears two counters.

name: decay_intensity_write_tables
description: When a global counter exceeds 25, derives two intensity bytes from two stored values and writes table bytes into two structures while their indices are nonzero. It decrements both intensity values with a floor of zero and clears the active flag when either reaches zero.

name: clear_table_and_init_parameters
description: Calls the shared setup routine with a global pointer table and clears the state byte of each entry in a sentinel-terminated pointer table. It sets two parameters to four below a global threshold of 23 or to called routine results modulo five above it, then sets a countdown to 40 and clears a second countdown.

name: update_lighting_parameters_and_table
description: While the active flag is set, toggles a state byte when a value passes 63 and writes a cycling value from zero to two into four structures. It also steps a countdown-driven index, clamps a second value between zero and 70, and writes that value divided by eight into a structure, cycling a table index when the value reaches zero.

name: fill_random_word_table
description: Fills 105 consecutive words with a linear congruential sequence starting from the seed 101, multiplying by 5701, adding 14977 and storing each result modulo 625. It has no branches and no known callers, since the entry is unreached.

name: draw_clipped_sprite_records
description: Walks a table of 24-byte sprite records, skipping records outside the visible window. For each visible record it clips the horizontal span and programs the blitter to draw its rows from the record's pixel data, choosing per column between two blitter control settings.

name: draw_sprite_records_with_offset
description: Shifts the sprite drawing by the difference between a stored position and the current one, then walks the same 24-byte sprite records. It clips each record's span to the shifted window and programs the blitter to draw its rows, calling a routine before and after the pass.

name: initialize_sprite_record_position
description: Computes screen x and y from two index arguments scaled by 160 with an offset of four plus global offsets, then stores them and clears several fields of the record. It writes a fixed control value, sends eight words through a loop that waits on the blitter busy flag, and finishes by storing a value computed from the second index.

name: init_icon_sprite_pointers
description: Sets four global pointers to offsets from a base address, then calls routines tied to the icons and screen sprite graphics files named in its referenced text. It stores two returned values in globals and finishes with one more call using fixed arguments.

name: store_offset_coordinates_and_flag
description: Stores the low word of the first argument, the high word minus a global base value, and the low word of the second argument into three globals. It then calls a routine with the argument one.

name: store_coordinates_and_call_zero
description: Stores the low word of the first argument, the high word minus the same global base value, and the low word of the second argument into three globals. It then calls a routine with the argument zero.

name: store_four_word_arguments
description: Copies the low and high words of two 32-bit arguments into four consecutive global variables. It makes no calls.

name: copy_table_block_to_buffer
description: For an index argument other than minus one, selects a source table and destination buffer from a flag in the argument's high word, then copies seventeen 32-byte chunks from the table entry at that index. If the entry's flag bit is set, it calls two routines instead.

name: expand_indices_through_lookup_table
description: Loops 68 times, and on each pass reads four index bytes from the source and uses each one to look up a byte in a global table. The four looked-up bytes are written to the destination in order.

name: expand_indices_with_counted_loop
description: Alternate entry into the index-expansion loop that takes its starting index from a register and a constant. It repeats a counted pass that writes four table-looked-up bytes per step until the count register reaches minus one.

name: build_pointer_table_swap_buffers
description: Fills six entries of a pointer table with addresses computed from a 4-bit index field and a base table, then swaps two buffer pointers and calls a routine. It swaps a second pair of buffer pointers, calls the routine again, then fills two entries per pass from a source index, writing fixed constants when the index is minus one and computed pointers otherwise.

name: fill_sprite_control_entries
description: When the index argument is minus one, writes four fixed header entries and clears their trailing fields. Otherwise it clips a horizontal span against a window of 167 and writes four entries whose addresses step by 136 bytes, each with a position and size word, returning the last address.

name: advance_cycle_and_dispatch_routines
description: Calls a routine with a value derived from a global, then advances a global cycle index that wraps at twelve. When the first argument is positive it computes a quotient from the argument's two fields and passes derived values to a routine, then calls a routine with a base global.

name: draw_visible_records_with_blitter
description: Walks a list of 14-word records, skipping inactive or off-screen entries and clipping each visible record's horizontal span. For each visible record it programs the blitter with fixed masks and control values, calls a routine repeatedly until it reports completion, stores the record pointer and returns a flag.

name: wait_and_store_register_values
description: Waits until a busy bit in a status byte is clear, then stores five register values into fixed offsets of a structure: three long words, a second copy of one of them, and a word.

name: walk_display_list_and_blit
description: Walks a linked list of display records by following each record's next pointer, and computes clipped source and destination offsets for every visible record. For each visible record it waits for the blitter and programs its masks, control, size and destination pointer.

name: store_argument_as_global_word
description: Stores the low 16 bits of its argument into a global variable and returns.

name: reset_list_pointers_zero_heads
description: Copies one global pointer into a second and derives a third pointer by adding a stored offset. It then sets that offset to 6000, writes zero into the words at both pointers, and calls a routine.

name: traverse_linked_list_until_null
description: Starting from a global list head, repeatedly passes the current pointer to a routine and follows the pointer that routine returns, until the word at the current pointer is zero.

name: interpret_script_record_list
description: Walks a linked list of script records, executing each record's state. State one advances a step counter and recomputes two offsets from a called routine, state two counts a step counter down, and state three reads a token that loads pointers, values or step deltas. It stops when a list entry is empty.

name: collect_overlapping_boxes_into_list
description: Walks a linked list of objects and clamps each one's bounding box against the bounds of a linked entry. Where the boxes overlap it calls a routine with the overlap position and size, writes a zero terminator, and then calls a routine for each entry of a second pointer list.

name: forward_struct_fields_to_routine
description: Reads a long from one field, a long from a second field and a word from a third field of the structure passed in, then forwards them to a routine.

name: run_timed_sequence_with_flags
description: Runs a sequence of routine calls, skipping some steps according to bits in its second argument, and repeats a polling step until a returned value is nonzero. It returns zero when the first query succeeds, otherwise a global offset plus the final result.

name: compute_product_quotient_and_remainder
description: Multiplies the two 16-bit halves of its first argument, then divides the product by the low 16 bits of its second argument. It returns the remainder in the upper word and the quotient in the lower word.

name: check_flags_and_return_code
description: Calls a routine, then when bit 14 of its argument is set calls two routines in turn. It returns one or two as soon as one of them returns nonzero, and zero otherwise.

name: initialize_flag_bytes
description: Sets one global byte to zero, a second global to one, and a third global variable to one.

name: toggle_global_flag_around_call
description: Sets a global variable to one, calls a routine, then clears the variable back to zero.

name: store_param_and_call_routine
description: Stores the low word of its argument into a global variable and then calls a routine.

name: toggle_low_bit_global_a
description: Inverts the lowest bit of its argument and stores the result in one global variable, then returns.

name: toggle_low_bit_global_b
description: Inverts the lowest bit of its argument and stores the result in a second global variable, then returns.

name: store_argument_flag_call
description: Sets a global flag to one, stores the low word of its argument in a global variable, calls a routine, then clears the flag back to zero.

name: store_nonzero_argument_and_call
description: When the argument is nonzero, sets a global flag to one, stores the argument in a global variable, calls a routine, and then clears the flag. Otherwise it returns without action.

name: run_five_calls_if_set
description: When a global flag is nonzero, calls five routines in sequence, two of which are library call stubs that load a library base from a global and call functions at fixed offsets from it. Otherwise it returns.

name: run_three_calls_if_set
description: When a global variable is nonzero, calls three routines in sequence. Otherwise it returns without making any calls.

name: route_pending_value_channel
description: When the enable flag is nonzero, finds the first of three slots that is empty, calls a routine, and copies the pending global value into that slot's destination variable, clearing the pending value. If the enable flag is zero or all three slots are filled, it stores the pending value into the fourth slot and clears it.

name: dispatch_pending_to_matching_slot
description: Compares a pending global value with four slot values and calls a routine for the first slot that matches, then clears the pending value. It is tied to the audio channel address registers.

name: reset_audio_channel_state
description: Writes constants to the four audio channels' registers, including volume and length settings, and enables DMA through a control write. It then clears the channel state variables, including the four slot values.

name: initialize_entity_slots_from_table
description: Saves a flag, sets it to one, and clears a block of 205 words of memory. When an index argument is nonzero it loads four pointers from a table entry and resets eight pointer slots to the global block, then writes the values two through eight into seven slots and restores the saved flag.

name: service_four_audio_slots
description: Returns at once when a global flag is set. Otherwise it checks four audio slots in turn and calls routines depending on whether each slot is occupied and on a mode byte and a pending-value flag.

name: forward_call_to_routine
description: Calls one routine and returns, with no other work in the pseudo-code.

name: load_table_long_clear_state
description: Reads a 32-bit value from a global table at an index taken from a global variable and stores it in another global variable. It then zeroes two global variables.

name: forward_call_audio_channel_zero
description: Calls one routine and returns, with no other work in the pseudo-code. Its only listed hardware reference is the audio channel zero address register, which the pseudo-code does not write directly.

name: forward_call_audio_routine_chain
description: Calls one routine and returns. The pseudo-code contains only a single call, so the other call targets listed for this routine are not visible here.

name: forward_single_call_wrapper
description: Calls one routine and returns, with no other work in the pseudo-code.

name: load_table_long_second_slot
description: Reads a 32-bit value from a global table at an index taken from a global variable and stores it in a second global variable. It then zeroes two global variables.

name: forward_call_audio_channel_one
description: Calls one routine and returns, with no other work in the pseudo-code. Its only listed hardware reference is the audio channel one address register, which the pseudo-code does not write directly.

name: forward_call_audio_chain_one
description: Calls one routine and returns. The pseudo-code contains only a single call, so the other call targets listed for this routine are not visible here.

name: pass_control_to_routine
description: Calls one routine and returns, with no other work in the pseudo-code.

name: load_table_long_clear_pair
description: Reads a 32-bit value from a global table at an index taken from another global variable and stores it in a third global variable. It then zeroes two global variables.

name: forward_call_audio_channel_two
description: Calls one routine and returns, with no other work in the pseudo-code. Its only listed hardware reference is the audio channel two address register, which the pseudo-code does not write directly.

name: forward_call_audio_chain_two
description: Calls one routine and returns. The pseudo-code contains only a single call, so the other call targets listed for this routine are not visible here.

name: delegate_to_single_routine
description: Calls one routine and returns without other operations.

name: load_table_long_index_reset
description: Reads a 32-bit value from a global table at an index taken from a global variable and stores it in another global variable. It then zeroes two more global variables.

name: forward_call_audio_channel_three
description: Calls one routine and returns, with no other work in the pseudo-code. Its only listed hardware reference is the audio channel three address register, which the pseudo-code does not write directly.

name: forward_call_audio_chain_three
description: Calls one routine and returns. The pseudo-code contains only a single call, so the other call targets listed for this routine are not visible here.

name: step_audio_channel_command_stream
description: Steps one audio channel record through its command stream. When its step counter is zero it reads the next command word, ending the stream on a zero word, and loads its length and envelope fields. Otherwise it counts down and adjusts the volume or period, then writes the channel's sample pointer and output values.

name: start_audio_channel_stream
description: Starts an audio channel record by loading its step counter from the first stream word, pointing it at the stream and clearing its output slot. It then writes the next sample value to the channel's output, applying an offset when a mode flag is set.

name: start_audio_channel_from_command
description: Reads the first word of a command stream and returns if it is zero. Otherwise it loads the channel's step counter and stream pointer, marks its state fields, and writes the next sample value to the channel's output, applying an offset when a mode flag is set.

name: clear_port_bit_start_channel
description: Clears bit one of the CIA port-A data register, which holds the joystick fire button and disk status bits, then starts an audio channel record from its first stream word as its sibling routine does.

name: set_port_bit_start_channel
description: Sets bit one of the CIA port-A data register, then starts an audio channel record from its first stream word as its sibling routines do.

name: load_channel_header_and_start
description: Copies a header from the stream into the channel record: a zero first word loads a pointer and a value directly, otherwise three long values are stored as channel fields. It then reads the command word and starts the channel as its sibling routines do when it is nonzero.

name: start_channel_from_pointer_table
description: Selects the next stream pointer from a per-channel pointer table, using the stored start address when the current entry is zero. It then reads the command word and starts the channel as its sibling routines do.

name: load_channel_pointer_and_start
description: Stores the long value at the stream pointer into a channel field and advances the channel's next-entry field past it. It then reads the command word and starts the channel as its sibling routines do.

name: copy_channel_pair_and_start
description: Copies two long values from the stream into channel fields, then reads a command word and starts the channel as its sibling routines do.

name: copy_channel_triple_and_start
description: Sets a channel flag to one, copies three long values from the stream into channel fields, then reads a command word and starts the channel as its sibling routines do.

name: clear_channel_counter_and_start
description: Clears a counter field of the channel record, then reads the command word from the stream and starts the channel as its sibling routines do.

name: clear_channel_flag_and_start
description: Clears a flag field of the channel record, then reads the command word from the stream and starts the channel as its sibling routines do.

name: release_slot_flag_by_type
description: Writes a global variable from a register argument. For a record whose type is six, five or seven it clears the matching slot flag, and otherwise clears a default slot flag. In each case it sets a global to one and clears the record's counter field.

name: clear_channel_zero_slot_state
description: Sets a global to one, writes a register argument into another global, clears the record's counter field and clears the slot flag for this channel. The listed hardware references are the audio channel zero period register and DMA control.

name: clear_channel_one_slot_state
description: Sets a global to one, writes a register argument into another global, clears the record's counter field and clears the slot flag for this channel. The listed hardware references are the audio channel one period register and DMA control.

name: clear_channel_two_slot_state
description: Sets a global to one, writes a register argument into another global, clears the record's counter field and clears the slot flag for this channel. The listed hardware references are the audio channel two period register and DMA control.

name: clear_channel_three_slot_state
description: Sets a global to one, writes a register argument into another global, clears the record's counter field and clears the slot flag for this channel. The listed hardware references are the audio channel three period register and DMA control.

name: set_channel_mode_start
description: Sets a mode flag field of the channel record to one, then reads the command word from the stream and starts the channel as its sibling routines do.

name: reset_idle_counters_and_call
description: When a global variable is zero, clears four global counters, sets another counter to ten, and calls a routine. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: run_three_calls_when_idle
description: When a global variable is zero, calls three routines in sequence. Otherwise it returns without making any calls.

name: update_mode_states_and_timers
description: When an enable flag is set and no gate is held, it chooses one of two mode states from a position value or a status flag and calls routines when the mode changes. It also decrements a timer that reloads to 20 when an event fires, and a countdown that reloads to 75 when it expires.

name: copy_zero_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from a source string into a destination buffer, including the terminating zero byte, and returns the destination pointer.

name: measure_zero_terminated_string
description: Walks a zero-terminated byte string to its terminator and returns the number of bytes before it. It does not change memory.

name: compare_zero_terminated_strings
description: Compares two byte strings one byte at a time up to a fixed length limit. It returns minus one or one at the first differing byte depending on which byte is smaller, and zero when the strings match up to the terminator or the limit.

name: forward_argument_to_routine
description: Passes its argument unchanged to another routine and returns, with no other work in the pseudo-code.

name: open_file_into_handle_table
description: Finds a free entry in a table of open file records, then uses the DOS library wrappers for Lock, Open, Seek, Write, Close and DeleteFile to open or create the named file. Flag bits in the second argument select the path taken, and the handle and flags are stored in the table entry, or an error code is recorded with a return of minus one on failure.

name: read_file_and_check_error
description: The pseudo-code could not be decompiled. Its listed calls are the DOS Read and IoErr wrappers, so it reads from a file and checks the DOS error code, and it is called from two places.

name: open_dos_library_or_alert
description: Opens the DOS library through the system library base and calls a routine when that succeeds, or raises a system alert when it fails. It first calls a supervisor function when a flag bit in the system structure is set, and stores the system base and the open result in globals.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Does nothing and returns immediately, with no work beyond the return.

name: allocate_manx_object_record
description: Allocates a fixed-size record and returns early if the allocation fails. Otherwise it initializes the record's fields, writes the identifier MANX into a global slot, and either links the record to a parent structure or sets flag bits on it, depending on a field of the parent. Its listed calls include the DOS current-directory, input, open and output wrappers.

name: split_command_line_into_arguments
description: Copies a command string into a buffer, then splits it into words on spaces, tabs and line breaks. Double-quoted arguments are honoured, with a doubled quote treated as an escaped quote, and the routine allocates an array of pointers to the words, ending it with a null pointer.

name: concatenate_string_with_limit
description: Appends a source string to the end of a destination string, copying at most a fixed number of bytes and adding a terminator if the copy is cut short. It returns the destination pointer.

name: append_string_with_count
description: Appends a source string to a destination string, copying at most the count given in its third argument, and adds a terminator when the count cuts the copy short. It returns the destination pointer.

name: copy_string_padded_to_count
description: Copies a source string into a destination buffer for at most the count given in its third argument, stopping at the terminator. It then fills the remaining bytes of the count with zeros and returns the destination pointer.

name: multiply_halves_32_bit_product
description: Multiplies two 32-bit register values by combining the cross products of their 16-bit halves. It returns the 32-bit product in the low register alongside the second argument.

name: open_icon_library_store_entry
description: Opens the icon library by name through the system library base, and on success looks up a function entry in the library and stores it with a second value in a structure. It also calls the DOS open wrapper, and its referenced text names the WINDOW and icon.library strings.

name: negate_result_for_mixed_signs
description: Calls a routine with its two arguments, then negates the result when exactly one of the arguments is negative. It returns that result together with the second argument.

name: apply_sign_to_routine_result
description: Calls a routine and negates its result when exactly one of its two inputs is negative, returning the result with the second input. Its body matches the routine at the adjacent address.

name: negate_result_when_first_negative
description: Calls a routine, then negates the returned value when the first argument is negative, and returns it with the second argument. The routine is reached through a gap in the decoded code, so it has no other known callers.

name: forward_call_single_target
description: Calls one routine and returns, with no other work in the pseudo-code.

name: divide_32_bit_with_remainder
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a 32-bit divisor and returns the quotient and remainder together. A divisor with a nonzero high word uses a 16-step shift-and-subtract loop, while a smaller divisor uses direct 16-bit divisions.

name: write_file_and_check_error
description: The pseudo-code could not be decompiled. Its listed calls are the DOS Write and IoErr wrappers, so it writes to a file and checks the DOS error code, and it is called from one place.

name: poll_signal_bit_result
description: Calls a function with a fixed mask and tests bit twelve of the result. When that bit is set it returns the result if a global flag is zero, otherwise it calls a routine, and in all other cases it returns zero.

name: pass_global_block_four_bytes
description: Passes a global variable with a size of four to a routine, passes the returned value to a second routine, then calls a third routine. Its listed calls include the DOS output and write wrappers.

name: call_hook_then_forward
description: Calls a global function pointer when it is set, then calls one more routine. When the pointer is clear, only the routine call is made.

name: run_cleanup_for_global_handles
description: Makes a counted series of routine calls over a global list, then calls a global hook when it is set. It runs a routine for each of several global handles that is set, calls a supervisor function when a flag bit in the system structure is set, and finishes with a routine call on a pointer pair.

name: close_file_table_slot
description: Closes the file in the table slot selected by its argument, calling the DOS Close wrapper unless a flag bit in the slot is set. It then clears the slot and returns zero, or records an error code and returns minus one when the index is out of range or the slot is empty.

name: call_unlock_via_library_base
description: Makes one indirect call through a vector read from a global library base. Its listed call is the DOS UnLock wrapper, and the decompiler could not resolve the target.

name: call_library_function_via_base
description: Makes one indirect call to a library function through a library base held in a global variable. The decompiler could not resolve the target, so the function is not named here.

name: allocate_object_record_with_fields
description: Finds a free index first and returns zero when none is free. Otherwise it allocates a 34-byte record, fills its pointer and flag fields from the arguments, stores the result of a library call, and passes the record to a routine before returning it.

name: release_object_record_chain
description: Releases a record by first calling a routine on the same record when its link field is nonzero. It then sets the state byte to minus one, clears a four-byte field to minus one, and calls two routines with the record's index and a fixed code. The entry is not reached in the decoded code, so it has no known callers.

name: forward_argument_with_fixed_code
description: Passes its argument together with the fixed value 48 to another routine and returns.

name: forward_argument_unreached_wrapper
description: Passes its argument to another routine and returns. The entry is not reached in the decoded code, so it has no known callers.

name: allocate_typed_record_for_pointer
description: Returns zero when its first argument is zero. Otherwise it allocates a record with a fixed flag value, returning zero if allocation fails, and on success sets the record's type byte to five, stores the high word of the second argument in it, and stores the first argument as a pointer field.

name: reset_record_and_release
description: Returns zero when its argument is zero. Otherwise it sets the record's state byte to minus one, sets two four-byte fields to minus one, and returns the result of a routine called with a word field from the record.

name: reset_record_state_fields
description: Sets the record's state byte to minus one and two four-byte fields to minus one, then calls a routine.

name: call_library_function_no_args
description: Makes one indirect call to a library function through a library base held in a global variable, with no arguments set in this routine. The decompiler could not resolve the call target, so the function is not named here.

name: call_library_function_from_base
description: Makes one indirect call to a library function through a library base held in a global variable, at a different vector from its neighbour. The decompiler could not resolve the call target.

name: dispatch_through_library_base
description: Makes one indirect call through a vector read from a library base held in a global variable. The decompiler could not resolve the call target.

name: dispatch_library_vector_call
description: Makes one indirect call through a vector read from a library base held in a global variable. Its listed library call is another vector, and the routine is called from two places.

name: fill_pointer_chain_header
description: Stores the address of its pointer argument into the memory it points to, adds four to that stored value, clears the next word of the block, and stores the original pointer in the word after that.

name: dispatch_library_function_pointer
description: Makes one indirect call through a library vector held in a global base. Its listed library call is another vector, and the decompiler could not resolve the target.

name: call_secondary_library_function
description: Makes one indirect call through a library base held in a different global variable, to a function at a fixed offset that the decompiler could not resolve. It is called from one place.

description: The entry is only a stub or bad data: the decoded instructions are a trap sequence that reflects decoding artefacts, so no routine behaviour is described.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Does nothing and returns immediately; the decoded body is only a return, so no behaviour is described.

name: configure_disk_sync_and_interrupts
description: Writes the interrupt and DMA control registers with bit fifteen set to enable and clear to disable, sets the disk sync word and disk pointer, and calls routines including a poll on a global flag. It then writes the disk and ADKCON control values and calls a routine for the block that follows. The copy loop after the allocation check is guarded by a flag that is always set, so it never runs in this code.

name: allocate_and_copy_disk_block
description: Clears and sets a CIA control bit around calls to routines, then calls the system memory allocator and checks its result. The copy into the allocated memory is guarded by a flag that is always set, so the copy loop never runs in this code. It then writes the disk sync word and DMA values into custom registers.

name: set_flag_bit_count_loop
description: Clears and then sets bit zero of a byte reached through a pointer, then runs a counted loop of 47 passes, each with an inner wait on a byte at a fixed offset. The inner wait compares the byte with itself in the decompiled form, so only the counted structure is reliable.

name: wait_on_counted_loop_status
description: Runs a loop over a count taken from a register, with an inner wait on a byte at a fixed offset. The inner wait compares the byte with itself in the decompiled form, so only the counted structure is reliable.

name: scan_table_after_hardware_wait
description: Writes several custom control registers, then waits for a status bit with a fixed timeout and returns minus one on timeout. It then scans up to 5000 words of a table at a fixed offset for the value held in a register, returning its position counted from one, or minus one when there is no match.

name: scan_word_table_for_value
description: Writes a control register, then scans up to 5000 words of a table at a fixed offset for the value held in a register. It returns the position counted from one, or minus one when there is no match.
